passages.original: collecta iam illic malignantium synagoga decem diebus ad ecclesiam est uetitus accedere, dum aduersus tam sanctum uirum malitia se peruersa consumit. soporatis deinde consiliis omnibus, ubi libitum est, aduocatur. adest una cum Romanis clericis et Lucifero Sardiniae episcopo, conuentus, ut in Athanasium subscriberet, ait :
passages.english: When the synagogue of the malicious had already been gathered there, he was forbidden for ten days to approach the church, while their perverse malice exhausted itself against so holy a man. Then, when all their counsels had been laid to rest, he was summoned at their pleasure. He came, together with the Roman clergy and Lucifer, bishop of Sardinia, and being called upon to sign against Athanasius, he said:
passages.notes: The passage ends at a colon; the words Eusebius spoke follow beyond the excerpt. 'Soporatis … consiliis omnibus' (literally 'all counsels having been put to sleep') is obscure; it may mean that their plans had been settled or completed. 'Synagoga' is used pejoratively of the hostile bishops' assembly.
